Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates upper lobe predominant irregular cavitation and fibrotic changes with volume loss (evidenced by hilar elevation), which are classic radiographic features of reactivation tuberculosis; the "prior lung resection" likely refers to surgical management of previous TB or severe sequelae, making anti-tubercular therapy the most appropriate next step.
